name: Spectral Graph Sparsification
problem_statement: Construct a sparse reweighted subgraph approximating the quadratic form of a weighted undirected graph Laplacian.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Build a sparsifier from scratch or update a supplied initial sparsifier.

problem_inputs.name: edge_budget
problem_inputs.description: Optional target edge count; heuristic methods must report attained quality.

problem_inputs.name: update_stream
problem_inputs.description: Optional explicitly ordered insertions/deletions for dynamic algorithms.

problem_inputs.name: initial_sparsifier
problem_inputs.description: Required in dynamic_updates mode. Weighted subgraph on the same vertex set; includes its declared quality guarantee or diagnostics.

required_outputs.name: sparsifier
required_outputs.description: Reweighted subset of input edges on the same vertices.

required_outputs.name: quality_summary
required_outputs.description: Measured/guaranteed spectral bounds, edge count, and verification method.

solution_semantics.objective: Reduce edge count while preserving x^T L x across vectors x within the declared guarantee.
solution_semantics.exactness: Distinguish proved bounds, probabilistic guarantees and empirical diagnostics; sampled-vector tests do not certify all-vector bounds.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Every sparsifier edge belongs to the current input graph and has nonnegative weight.
Preserve connected components when claiming a nontrivial spectral approximation.
Use generalized eigenvalues on small graphs to verify claimed spectral error.
Dynamic-update mode requires an initial sparsifier and an update stream; validate the result against the final updated graph.
Report preprocessing and initialization cost separately from incremental-update cost.
edge_cases: Bridge removal violates a nontrivial spectral guarantee.

correctness: Every sparsifier edge belongs to the current input graph and has nonnegative weight.
Preserve connected components when claiming a nontrivial spectral approximation.
Use generalized eigenvalues on small graphs to verify claimed spectral error.
